title: Take a Further Step Beyond Data Augmentation: Augmented Knowledge Purification for Federated Recommendation

problem.claim: Federated sequential recommendation suffers from severe data sparsity because users' item interaction sequences are typically short.

gap.claim: Common data augmentation operators generate additional noise and lead to unstable performance.

contributions.claim: FR-AKP performs augmented knowledge purification after data augmentation at both intra-client and inter-client levels.
At the intra-client level, FR-AKP uses Fast Fourier Transform and personalized frequency selection to denoise augmented local data.

At the inter-client level, FR-AKP uses a fusion-network-based aggregation mechanism that generates personalized aggregation weights from distributional differences in clients' frequency-domain features.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four real-world datasets report that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods by up to 34.62% in Recall and 29.92% in NDCG.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated sequential recommendation provides recommendation services while preserving user data privacy.
Federated sequential recommendation faces severe data sparsity because user interaction sequences are short.
Data augmentation is commonly used to generate more sequences, but augmentation operators introduce noise and unstable performance.
FR-AKP purifies augmented knowledge through frequency-domain denoising within clients and personalized aggregation across clients.
The authors report improvements over state-of-the-art methods on four real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: Data augmentation can increase sequence quantity while also introducing noise and unstable performance.

interpretation.claim: Augmentation may require a purification or denoising step rather than being treated as uniformly beneficial.

application.claim: For sparse sequential recommendation, evaluate augmentation together with mechanisms that filter noisy augmented knowledge.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported approach generalizes beyond the described federated sequential recommendation setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four datasets, baselines, or experimental protocols.
The abstract does not provide ablation results or details about the frequency selection and fusion network.
The abstract does not report computational cost, privacy guarantees, or statistical significance procedures.
